answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, non-transferable stake that is slashed for misbehaviour, rather than counting free accounts. Like an orchard where every tree must be planted and tended before it bears fruit, each agent earns reputation only through verified work over time. A walnut grower cannot fake a harvest by planting a thousand seedlings overnight; the ridge between cheap creation and earned standing is time plus forfeitable stake, so spawning sock-puppets costs more than any reward they could extract.
